# Events & Cancellation

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index.

**Coverage**: 3/3 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 0/3 (0%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EventTarget` / `addEventListener` / `dispatchEvent` | ✅ | • Single-target dispatch — no DOM tree, so no capture/bubble/propagation (`stopPropagation` is a no-op; `stopImmediatePropagation` halts the remaining listeners)<br>• `capture`/`passive`/`signal` options accepted but ignored (`signal` cancellation arrives with `AbortController`)<br>• No `class X extends EventTarget` (built-in `extends` targets are rejected) | • A bare `Map<string, listener-list>` reusing EventEmitter's registry + snapshot dispatch; `dispatchEvent` reads `event.type`, invokes each listener with the event object, and returns `!defaultPrevented` ([TDD-00081](../tdd/TDD-00081.md)/[ADR-00235](../adr/ADR-00235.md))<br>• `{ once }` is honored. `removeEventListener` matches by listener identity — a const-bound closure or a *named-function* reference both remove correctly; a listener may take 0 or 1 argument. See [ADR-00967](../adr/ADR-00967.md), [ADR-00969](../adr/ADR-00969.md) |
| `Event` / `CustomEvent` | ✅ | • The fuller WHATWG properties (`target`/`currentTarget`/`bubbles`/`composed`/`timeStamp`/`eventPhase`/`isTrusted`) are absent — V1 surface is `type`, `defaultPrevented`, `cancelable`, `CustomEvent.detail`<br>• `bubbles` in the `new Event(type, { … })` init is accepted but ignored (single-target dispatch)<br>• `stopPropagation()` is a no-op (single-target dispatch, no capture/bubble tree) | • Plain fixed-shape objects tagged `IsEvent`; construction + field reads + `preventDefault`/`stop*` work standalone. Dispatching them is `EventTarget` (next row) — [TDD-00081](../tdd/TDD-00081.md)/[ADR-00234](../adr/ADR-00234.md)<br>• `cancelable` is honored — `preventDefault()` sets `defaultPrevented` only on a cancelable event, a no-op otherwise ([ADR-00587](../adr/ADR-00587.md)); `CustomEvent.detail` type is inferred from the value |
| `AbortController` / `AbortSignal` | ✅ | • A manual `controller.abort(reason)` with a custom reason still makes the awaited fetch throw an `AbortError` DOMException rather than that reason value; DOMException carries no legacy numeric `.code`<br>• `AbortSignal.any(signals)` snapshots the input signals at construction — a source that aborts *after* the composite is built does not yet propagate to it (needs listener-closure wiring) | • `signal.onabort = cb` is supported ([ADR-00978](../adr/ADR-00978.md)): the event-handler property is a listener slot fired alongside the `addEventListener('abort', …)` listeners, sharing one `abort` event (so a `stopImmediatePropagation()` in `onabort` suppresses the rest); `signal.onabort = null` clears it and re-assigning replaces it<br>• `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` now aborts in the **background** at its deadline ([ADR-00979](../adr/ADR-00979.md)): the event loop / timer drain fire the abort (set `aborted`, a `TimeoutError` DOMException `reason`, and the listeners/`onabort`) once the deadline elapses while the loop is alive for other work, without ever keeping the loop alive on its own — a lone timeout or an early-completing `fetch(url, { signal })` exits immediately rather than waiting out the timeout (Node unref parity)<br>• `fetch(url, { signal })` cancellation works — pre-flight, mid-flight, and via **`AbortSignal.timeout(ms)`**, on both the top-level `await` path and the fiber path (a fetch awaited inside an `http.listen` handler): the await loop checks the signal every spin, and the event loop folds the timeout deadline into its `select()` wait so an idle loop wakes at the deadline — then tears the transfer down and throws a **`DOMException`** (`instanceof DOMException` and, since it inherits `Error`, `instanceof Error` both hold), named `AbortError` for a manual abort and `TimeoutError` for a timeout ([ADR-00237](../adr/ADR-00237.md)–[ADR-00240](../adr/ADR-00240.md))<br>• `new DOMException(message?, name?)` is constructible directly; `AbortSignal` is an object with `aborted`/`reason`/`deadlineNs` plus a hidden listener map — an EventTarget that fires `"abort"`; its pointer rides on the fetch's pending handle, and `__kml_signal_aborted` folds the timeout deadline in for the await loop, the event-loop resume scan, and the `select()` wait ([TDD-00081](../tdd/TDD-00081.md)/[ADR-00236](../adr/ADR-00236.md)–[ADR-00240](../adr/ADR-00240.md)) |
